Compare the tasks and tradeoffs.

Plain → extension in each example below. These are the creator’s reported observations in his configuration, not universal costs or a ranking.

Superpowers

04:07–06:35

A planning and development workflow.

Coding job 2: $0.32 → $0.37, but 7.6 → 5.1 min. Website: $2.84 → $5.15; 14 → 26 min.

What this result leaves open

Website first-pass wishes met: 63% → 100%. Final hidden-test scores: 100 → 100. The creator reported higher first-pass coverage with the higher spend.

Caveman

06:35–08:05

Shorter answers and tool output.

20 developer questions, each answered twice: $0.152 → $0.162 per answer; answer score 94.3 → 94.1 / 100.

What this result leaves open

The “answer concisely” control cost $0.113, with a lower 90.1 score. Shorter output alone did not establish better value. Today’s repository also includes a proxy; the clip tested a particular skill setup.

Graphify

08:09–10:23

A queryable codebase knowledge graph.

Textual session: $4.63 → $5.74; 12-question time 12.7 → 16.5 min; answer score 93.0 → 89.1 / 100.

What this result leaves open

Reported tokens read per question: 258K → 288K. Local mapping and Cloud are distinct; this test does not settle the Cloud service’s claims.

Claude-Mem

10:24–12:10

Persistent session context and retrieval.

Built-in memory → built-in plus Claude-Mem: $5.50 → $5.54 total. Scenario scores were equal: 1.00, 0.75, 1.00 on both sides (scale 0–1).

What this result leaves open

Three scenarios across three sessions. Equal scores include imperfect recall of a changed decision; they do not establish perfect memory or universal redundancy.

Separate evidence · SkillLantern · 9 Nov 2026

Our Motion pair is inspectable.

One synthetic reservation form, one output per condition. Both passed all 13 recorded browser checks, including validation, retry, keyboard flow, reduced motion and mobile layout. Generation cost and time were not measured.

No human preference study, screen-reader or physical-device benchmark. Native skill installation was not exercised. Passing these checks does not establish a design-quality improvement.

Run a fair comparison of your own.

  1. Choose a bounded task. Write acceptance checks before either run; use a disposable copy of the same project snapshot.
  2. Hold the setup steady. Same model, version, effort, permissions and necessary project rules. Fresh isolated sessions; change one optional extension.
  3. Measure the whole job. Include startup context, setup/background costs, elapsed time, first-pass coverage and human corrections. Repeat runs when affordable.
  4. Choose for your actual constraints. A faster or better first pass can justify extra cost. A tie on one task cannot settle every future task.
Sources, coverage & limits · reviewed 21 Nov 2026

Inspired by Chase AI’s 18-minute TikTok comparison (metadata upload date: 17 Nov 2026). We reviewed the full supplied captions and 24 sampled frames; no continuous watch or listening, and no benchmark reproduction. Website numbers above were checked against the 06:15 slide. Caption errors are possible; the slide reports 1,500 Textual files.

Original project links were checked 21 Nov 2026. Repositories can change after the version in the clip. No raw prompts, pinned versions, full run logs, grading rubrics or complete diffs were available; score calibration, dollar accounting and statistical confidence are unknown. The creator promotes a paid masterclass, which we did not assess.

Anthropic’s cost guidance supports inspecting context and configuration. Useful skills and hooks can still help; this page does not infer that every extension should be removed. Built-in memory is documented in Claude Code’s memory guide.
